name: Mirrodin
description: Mirrodin is an artificial metal plane lit by suns, created by Karn as Argentum and later conquered by Phyrexia and remade as New Phyrexia.

bio.text: Karn made the artificial plane of Argentum, and Memnarch, the guardian Karn left in charge, was corrupted by a drop of glistening oil and renamed it Mirrodin.

citations.text: "Why the Mirrans Will Endure". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 22 Feb 2011. Archived by the Internet Archive.
"Memnarch", section "Warden". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Memnarch", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: Memnarch terraformed the world, destroyed the ur-golems and abducted beings from other planes with soul traps to populate it.

citations.text: "Memnarch", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Why the Mirrans Will Endure". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 22 Feb 2011. Archived by the Internet Archive.

bio.text: Glissa Sunseeker defeated Memnarch as the fifth, green sun was born, and the Vanishing then returned the transplanted elders to their home planes while the younger generations stayed as the Mirrans.

citations.text: "Moreover: Doing Sequels Right". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 31 Aug 2010. Archived by the Internet Archive.
Channel the Suns (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.
"Why the Mirrans Will Endure". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 22 Feb 2011. Archived by the Internet Archive.

bio.text: Phyrexian oil that Karn had carried unknowingly planted a virus on the plane, and Phyrexia began rebuilding itself with Mirrodin as host.

citations.text: "Phyrexia and the Vaultlord". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 7 Sep 2010. Archived by the Internet Archive.
"Phyrexia and the Vaultlord". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 7 Sep 2010. Archived by the Internet Archive.

bio.text: The spread grew from a trickle of arrivals into a full invasion and a mutual slaughter with the Mirrans, who united under a single banner.

citations.text: "Why the Mirrans Will Endure". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 22 Feb 2011. Archived by the Internet Archive.

bio.text: Koth, Elspeth and Venser joined the resistance, and Venser gave his life and spark to Karn, freeing him from Phyrexian tyranny.

citations.text: "Venser", section "Quest for Karn". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Karn", section "Quest for Karn". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: The resistance was nonetheless lost, the Phyrexians took control of Mirrodin and renamed it New Phyrexia, and Koth escaped to Zhalfir with fewer than twenty Mirrans.

citations.text: "New Phyrexia", section "Set details". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"New Phyrexia", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Koth of the Hammer", section "Invasion of the Multiverse". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch takes over Mirrodin and sends the Ur-Golems against the mycosynth plague, which eradicates them.
timeline.quote: who sent them to fight the mycosynth plague that eventually eradicated them

citation.text: "Golem", section "Ur-Golems". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Karn reveals the Mirari's origins and takes it back to Argentum.
timeline.quote: Karn appeared and revealed the Mirari's humble origins and took it back to Argentum

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Glissa Sunseeker declares she will unlock the secret at the heart of Mirrodin.
timeline.quote: There's a secret at the heart of this world, and I will unlock it.

citation.text: Glissa Sunseeker (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Glissa says someone is defying the gods and shaping the planet, and she intends to stop it.
timeline.quote: Someone or something is defying the power of the gods and shaping this planet. I intend for it to stop.

citation.text: Tempest of Light (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: A leonin kha stuns a nim raider into kneeling.
timeline.quote: Stunned by the mere presence of the leonin kha, the nim raider quickly fell to its knees.

citation.text: Awe Strike (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: A nim is consumed in sunfire, leaving only molten iron.
timeline.quote: Within seconds, the nim was consumed in blinding sunfire.

citation.text: Soul Nova (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Raksha Golden Cub praises the skyhunters who raise the alarm against levelers.
timeline.quote: They are the first to raise the alarm when the levelers attack, and the first to risk their lives to defend the pride.

citation.text: Skyhunter Patrol (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Bosh searches for the secrets of his past while Glissa searches for the truth about Memnarch.
timeline.quote: As Glissa searches for the truth about Memnarch, Bosh searches to unearth the secrets of his past.

citation.text: Bosh, Iron Golem (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Ur-golem etchings tell of Memnarch's change from guardian to merciless god.
timeline.quote: The ur-golem runes tell of the transformation of Mirrodin's warden from silent guardian to merciless god.

citation.text: Tower of Champions (Mirrodin, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Some atogs are transported from Dominaria to Mirrodin where they become alpha predators.
timeline.quote: Some atogs were transported from Dominaria to the metallic plane of Mirrodin

citation.text: "Atog", section "Mirrodin/New Phyrexia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Bruenna agrees to help Glissa, Slobad and Bosh reach the Pool of Knowledge.
timeline.quote: she agreed to assist them, motivated by the opportunity to undermine the Vedalken

citation.text: "Bruenna", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Bruenna and Glissa are captured by Lord Pontifex, escape, and survive a confrontation with Janus.
timeline.quote: She was later captured with Glissa by Lord Pontifex

citation.text: "Bruenna", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Bruenna unites the races of Mirrodin with Glissa and Lyese against Memnarch.
timeline.quote: Bruenna was instrumental in bridging alliances between elves, leonin, goblins, and others.

citation.text: "Bruenna", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Bruenna loses a hand in the war and later frees Glissa from stasis.
timeline.quote: Bruenna lost a hand during the war with Memnarch

citation.text: "Bruenna", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Slobad relinquishes his spark, triggering the Vanishing and recovering the souls.
timeline.quote: those souls were recovered when Slobad relinquished his fresh spark

citation.text: "Bruenna", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Krark finds a way into Mirrodin's depths and another world there, per legend.
timeline.quote: Krark was a goblin who, legend states, found a way into the depths of Mirrodin and found another world there.

citation.text: "Goblin", section "Krark-Clan". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Phyrexians launch their initial assault on Mirrodin and its divided tribes fall one after another, the Morioks first.
timeline.quote: The Morioks fell first, followed by the Neuroks, and finally the Sylvoks.

citation.text: "Human", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Only the Aurioks and Vulshoks hold some ground against the Phyrexians, and their populations are still decimated.
timeline.quote: Only the Aurioks and Vulshoks managed to hold any of their ground, and their populations were still decimated.

citation.text: "Human", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Karn leaves Argentum to train Jeska, granting his warden the Mirari orb and stewardship of the plane.
timeline.quote: The second was stewardship over the plane itself.

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Warden". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: A spot of glistening oil catches Memnarch's eye and he wipes it away, beginning the Corruption of Memnarch.
timeline.quote: the Corruption of Memnarch had now begun.

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Warden". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch renames the world Mirrodin, terraforms it and destroys the ur-golems, then begins abducting inhabitants of other planes.
timeline.quote: His first act was to rename the world Mirrodin , after his previous existence as the Mirari.

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch ingests blinkmoth serum, builds a serum tank body, and dreams of becoming a planeswalker.
timeline.quote: Memnarch dreamed of becoming a planeswalker.

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch finds Glissa and becomes obsessed with stealing her spark; she escapes his agents repeatedly.
timeline.quote: becoming obsessed with capturing her and stealing her spark for himself.

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: During the Leveler War the Mephidross advances into other territories until Memnarch is put down.
timeline.quote: until the mad guardian was put down

citation.text: "Mephidross", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: As Phyrexia advances the Dross swallows parts of the Tangle and Razorgrass Fields while the Seven Steel Thanes vie for control.
timeline.quote: jockeying for control over the swamplands

citation.text: "Mephidross", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Mirrodin is compleated into New Phyrexia and the Mephidross is siphoned into the Dross Pits.
timeline.quote: siphoned out entirely into a new layer within Phyrexia, the Dross Pits

citation.text: "Mephidross", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Karn reshapes the Mirari into the sentient Memnarch, protector of Argentum.
timeline.quote: Karn reshaped the Mirari as a sentient being

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Memnarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch renames the plane Mirrodin.
timeline.quote: renamed the plane Mirrodin

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Memnarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: After Memnarch's defeat Karn melts him down, revealing the Mirari, left in the care of Glissa, Slobad and Geth.
timeline.quote: Karn returned to his plane and melted down Memnarch to his core, revealing the Mirari underneath.

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Memnarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Glissa begins her story, setting out to find out why the levelers seek to destroy her, which starts to uncover the mysteries of Mirrodin.
timeline.quote: begins her story to find out why the monstrous "levelers" seek to destroy her

citation.text: "Mirrodin", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch destroys the Neurok settlement of Medev.
timeline.quote: Medev was a prominent Neurok settlement until its destruction by the planar caretaker Memnarch .

citation.text: "Neurok", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: After the Vanishing, the Synod claims all serum and the Neurok form secret networks to undermine the Vedalken.
timeline.quote: They began to form secret sects to undermine the Vedalken.

citation.text: "Neurok", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Neurok use the Litera Phials to learn how to destroy vedalken drones.
timeline.quote: even learning the secret to destroy a key vedalken weapon

citation.text: "Neurok", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Neurok and Vedalken leaders agree to an uneasy truce.
timeline.quote: Leaders between the Neurok and the Vedalken reached an uneasy truce.

citation.text: "Neurok", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Karn's leaked Phyrexian oil corrupts Memnarch and Mirrodin, giving rise to New Phyrexia under five praetors.
timeline.quote: The five praetors of New Phyrexia now control the plane

citation.text: "Phyrexia", section "Phyrexian resurrection". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Karn creates Mirrodin and inadvertently drips Phyrexian oil on it, leaving Memnarch as guardian.
timeline.quote: he inadvertently dripped a small amount of the corrupting Phyrexian oil on his perfect world

citation.text: "Phyrexia", section "Phyrexia on Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Karn uses the Mirari's core to create Memnarch, protector of the artificial plane of Argentum.
timeline.quote: the planeswalker Karn used the Mirari’s core to create Memnarch

citation.text: "Rift Era", section "Creation and Corruption of Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Glistening oil corrupts Memnarch, who abducts organic beings from other planes to seed Mirrodin.
timeline.quote: he began abducting organic beings from other planes to seed life on Mirrodin

citation.text: "Rift Era", section "Creation and Corruption of Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Slobad is born under the Eye of Doom, a taboo meaning death, but his mother hides him in the air ducts.
timeline.quote: Slobad's mother did not follow tradition and instead hid the young goblin in the air ducts

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Exile". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Dwugget finds the infant Slobad and raises him in the Krark Cult.
timeline.quote: the infant goblin was found by another goblin by the name of Dwugget.

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Exile". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Leonin capture Slobad and make him a servant of their leader Raksha.
timeline.quote: he was captured by the Leonin and turned into a servant

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Exile". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Slobad flees after a failed invention and finds the levelers' cavern.
timeline.quote: Slobad decided it was best to flee before any punishment could be forthcoming

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Exile". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Slobad repairs the golem Bosh, who joins Glissa and Slobad.
timeline.quote: introduced himself as Bosh

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Glissa kills Pontifex, who was orchestrating the attacks.
timeline.quote: Glissa confronted the mysterious individual orchestrating the attacks

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The group learns Memnarch is responsible for the attacks.
timeline.quote: The ancient and mythical being known as Memnarch was responsible for the attacks.

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Kaldra avatar betrays the group when Memnarch takes control of it.
timeline.quote: they were betrayed by the avatar when Memnarch gained control of it.

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Bosh stays behind and gives his life so his friends can escape.
timeline.quote: Bosh stayed behind while the pair escaped, giving his life to spare his friends.

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Fifth Dawn is triggered and a new green sun is born.
timeline.quote: The Fifth Dawn was triggered, blasting the Kaldra Guardian away

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Viridian Elves arrest Glissa and Slobad for the murder of Glissa's parents.
timeline.quote: were immediately arrested by the Viridian Elves for the murder of Glissa's parents

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Glissa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch captures Slobad, tortures him, amputates his limbs and links him to a machine.
timeline.quote: Slobad was captured without much fight and Memnarch made plans to utilize the goblin's brilliance.

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Imprisonment". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Glissa knocks herself and Memnarch into the core and her spark transfers to Slobad.
timeline.quote: her spark was accidentally transferred to his battered form

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Imprisonment". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Slobad meets Karn, the creator of Mirrodin.
timeline.quote: he came face to face with the planeswalker who had created Mirrodin itself: Karn

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Imprisonment". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Slobad gives up the spark to resurrect the dead and send them home.
timeline.quote: the goblin gave up the spark to resurrect all the people killed on Mirrodin and send them home

citation.text: "Slobad", section "Imprisonment". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Glissa has a vision while hunting a vorrac with Kane and distrusts the trolls' memory-erasing ceremony.
timeline.quote: She believes her visions are repressed memories that are key to the elves' past

citation.text: "The Moons of Mirrodin", section "Glissa's vision". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: On Mirrodin, the mycosynth's vapor mutates the vedalken, who develop four arms and gills.
timeline.quote: the mycosynth created a vapor that induced mutations in the vedalken

citation.text: "Vedalken", section "Mirrodin/New Phyrexia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: After Memnarch's fall, the Synod reorganizes the vedalken into sanctives, and Neurok revolts force cooperation.
timeline.quote: revolts from the Neurok forced the two races into a state of cooperation rather than subservience

citation.text: "Vedalken", section "Mirrodin/New Phyrexia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: After Memnarch's defeat the nim are briefly inert and many are killed by the Moriok.
timeline.quote: the Nim were briefly rendered inert, and many were killed by the Moriok

citation.text: "Zombie", section "Mirrodin/New Phyrexia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The reawakened nim slaughter the Moriok in the Nim Onslaught.
timeline.quote: they began slaughtering Moriok in an event later known as the Nim Onslaught or Nim Massacre.

citation.text: "Zombie", section "Mirrodin/New Phyrexia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Ushanti recounts a vision of the end of times in which all leonin are torn from the world.
timeline.quote: I have seen the end of times, a future in which all our kind are torn from this world.

citation.text: Soulscour (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch grants the vedalken a touch of his power in exchange for service, creating a debt.
timeline.quote: Memnarch shared a touch of his power with the vedalken in return for their service.

citation.text: Synod Artificer (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch created the myr with dependability, controllability and disposability in mind.
timeline.quote: Memnarch created the myr with three qualities in mind: dependability, controllability, and disposability.

citation.text: Myr Moonvessel (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch finds madness between metal and flesh.
timeline.quote: In the blur between metal and flesh, Memnarch found madness.

citation.text: Memnarch (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch separated the Ur-Golem's eye from its body millennia ago.
timeline.quote: It still stares accusingly at Memnarch, though millennia have passed since he separated the eye from its body.

citation.text: Ur-Golem's Eye (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch escalates the stakes when civilizations develop ways to fight the levelers.
timeline.quote: When Mirrodin's varied civilizations developed ways to fight the levelers, Memnarch upped the stakes.

citation.text: Eater of Days (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Mirrodin begins to take on a life of its own through Memnarch's work.
timeline.quote: In bringing life to Mirrodin, Memnarch was more successful than he knew—for Mirrodin began to take on a life of its own.

citation.text: Tanglewalker (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch is quoted on the equilibrium of his experimental myr population.
timeline.quote: As the experimental population grows, so do the number of myr. It's a perfect equilibrium.

citation.text: Genesis Chamber (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Korva reacts to a fire.
timeline.quote: Now I'm thirsty.

citation.text: Flamebreak (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Glissa Sunseeker recalls Slobad as seemingly exiled for being too smart.
timeline.quote: I used to joke that he had been exiled for being too smart.

citation.text: Slobad, Goblin Tinkerer (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Slobad wonders what kind of ogre approaches.
timeline.quote: Is it the stomping kind or the munching kind?

citation.text: Drooling Ogre (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Durg is about to be blown away.
timeline.quote: Always easily impressed, Durg was about to be blown away.

citation.text: Goblin Archaeologist (Darksteel, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Chunth entrusts Glissa with the secret that the world is hollow before a traitor kills him.
timeline.quote: This is the secret that Chunth , the Tel-Jilad troll elder, entrusts to Glissa before his death at the hands of a traitor.

citation.text: "Darksteel", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Fleeing her vedalken pursuers, Glissa discovers that Memnarch is real and waits for her.
timeline.quote: Memnarch is real, and he patiently waits for the elvish champion to find him.

citation.text: "Darksteel", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Memnarch's plan is revealed: he will use the green sun's power and Glissa's spark to become a planeswalker, as Mirrodin comes undone.
timeline.quote: He has built the Panopticon on the exact spot the green sun will emerge from to use its power and turn himself into a planeswalker .

citation.text: "The Darksteel Eye", section "Memnarch's plan revealed". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Raksha admits that even as kha she is nothing without her people.
timeline.quote: I may be kha, but without my soldiers, my people, I am nothing.

citation.text: Leonin Squire (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Ushanti prophesies that guardians will be needed more than ever.
timeline.quote: If what I have seen comes to pass, we will need our guardians more than ever.

citation.text: Skyhunter Prowler (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch muses on taking Mirrodin apart and beginning again.
timeline.quote: Perhaps I should take Mirrodin apart and begin again.

citation.text: Into Thin Air (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch threatens to wipe all memory of a foe from reality.
timeline.quote: All memory of your existence will be wiped from reality. You will die, and no one will mourn.

citation.text: Door to Nothingness (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Memnarch boasts that everything flows through him.
timeline.quote: It is all in my grasp.

citation.text: Fist of Suns (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The fifth sun is born, seen as doom by some and salvation by others.
timeline.quote: To some the birth of the fifth sun was a sign of doom.

citation.text: Channel the Suns (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The fifth sun joins the other four and awakens new abilities in Mirrodin's creatures.
timeline.quote: As the fifth sun joins the other four, new abilities awaken in the creatures of Mirrodin.

citation.text: Suntouched Myr (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Auriok salvagers gather scraps left by Memnarch and the vedalken.
timeline.quote: Memnarch or the vedalken salvage most of the large machines, leaving us only scraps.

citation.text: Auriok Salvagers (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Cosmic larvae finally end their wandering from plane to plane.
timeline.quote: For millennia they wandered from plane to plane, devouring all metal.

citation.text: Cosmic Larva (Fifth Dawn, 2004), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Glissa, Bosh and Slobad journey to Mirrodin's core with the Kaldra avatar to confront Memnarch.
